channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic Shares Drop Post-Market on Apple’s AI Agent Plans
item.description: Shares of Anthropic PBC fell more than 3% in after-hours trading following their New York debut, as Apple Inc. plans to develop an autonomous AI agent and investor caution over the AI trade weighed on momentum throughout the day.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu

item.title: Could a Jensen Huang-Style Scandal Happen at Apple?
item.description: On the Power On podcast, Joanna Stern joins Mark Gurman to discuss Nvidia’s leadership fallout, Apple’s executive culture under Steve Jobs and Tim Cook and why Cupertino isn’t immune. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Currency Playbook Gets Rewritten in Asia as Losers Bounce Back
item.description: A trade that drove Asian currencies for much of this year is starting to turn, as oil prices retreat and investors slash exposure to the artificial-intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wong

item.title: The City at the Center of AI
item.description:
Anthropic’s record-setting IPO is expected to make many of its employees rich, and other AI companies may be next. At the center of this modern gold rush is San Francisco, a city used to booms and busts – but never at this scale.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Propagate Co-CEO on New Sam Bankman-Fried Docuseries
item.description: Ben SIlverman, Propagate Co-CEO & Chairman, discusses Sam Bankman-Fried’s early investment in Anthropic, which he could not benefit from after FTX and Alameda Research were forced to sell their reported $500 million stake before FTX’s collapse. As Anthropic made its trading debut, executive producer Ben Silverman said the IPO reinforced that Bankman-Fried had a strong investing thesis, but compared his rise and fall to Icarus flying too high. Silverman speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s Historic IPO Debuts
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Class V Group Founder Lise Buyer, Menlo Ventures Partner Matt Murphy, GIC Head of Technology Investment Group Chris Emanuel, Goldman Sachs Chief Credit Strategist Amanda Lynam, Robinhood Markets CIO Stephanie Guild, Warrington College of Business Administration IPO Initiative Director Jay Ritter, Center for a New American Security Senior Fellow & Director Emily Kilcrease, Sony Interactive Entertainment America Former President & CEO Shawn Layden, & Propagate Co-CEO & Chairman Ben Silverman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Cloud CEO Hits ‘Rock Bottom’ in Race to Survive Chip Crisis
item.description: In little more than a month, Aolani Cloud Pte Chief Executive Officer Nicholas Chia has watched his industry go from boom to dangerously close to bust.
item.dc:creator: David Ramli, Gao Yuan and Sheryl Tian Tong Lee

item.title: CATL, Innolight May Join Hong Kong Tech Index in Major AI Revamp
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. and Zhongji Innolight Co. are among shares expected to join Hong Kong’s technology stock benchmark in a major overhaul, helping the gauge better capture the artificial intelligence boom and compete with Asian rivals.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Yang

item.title: Former Playstation Exec. On ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Debut
item.description: Shawn Layden, Former President and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America and Former Chairman of PlayStation Worldwide Studios, calls the scale difficult to convey to people unfamiliar with games, saying GTA VI is not just a game but an economy in itself. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'GTA VI' Is a 'Booster Shot' for Gaming, Shawn Layden Says
item.description: Shawn Layden, former president and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America, says the Grand Theft Auto games are "planets of their own" during an interview on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lyft Airport Pickups Saw Double-Digit Gain During US Ground Stop
item.description: The US grounding of flights last Friday spurred a surge in demand for Lyft Inc.’s airport rideshare service, including longer-distance rides, as stranded passengers turned to ground transportation to get home or reach their destinations.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Anthropic Shares Jump 17% After $107.3 Billion IPO Breaks Record
item.description: Anthropic made its debut as a public company today — the first AI frontier lab to do so. Shares soared 17% above their IPO price in the biggest offering on record, raising $107.3 billion despite signs of growing caution around the artificial intelligence trade. Ed Ludlow explains what comes next (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GS Chief Credit Strategist on 2027 AI Financing Outlook
item.description: Amanda Lynam, Goldman Sachs Chief Credit Strategist, says hyperscalers issued debt early - starting in 2025, before their free cash flow turned negative - and that a recent surge pushed 2026 borrowing above Goldman’s forecast of $250 billion. For 2027, Goldman expects debt to finance 35% of hyperscaler capital spending, equivalent to about $440 billion. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: If You Want To Trade Like Anthropic, You Better Look Like Anthropic, Says Buyer
item.description: Lise Buyer, Founder of Class V Group and one of the chief architects of Google’s 2004 auction IPO, discusses Anthropic’s stronger-than-expected IPO demand, share count and pricing after reports had suggested a possible downsizing. She cautioned investors not to rely on market chatter, emphasizing that a company’s value is ultimately what investors are willing to pay. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California Probing If Nvidia Misled Investors on China Risks
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is being investigated by California officials to determine whether any of its actions resulted in advanced chips or confidential information being improperly obtained by China.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Menlo Makes First-Ever IPO Investment With Anthropic
item.description: Menlo Ventures Partner Matt Murphy explains why Anthropic became the first IPO the venture firm has ever invested in, calling it an “exceptional opportunity.” He discusses Anthropic’s compute strategy, the disruptive potential of Claude Code and the idea that the company is ultimately “selling intelligence” and the ability to innovate. Murphy also says Anthropic’s longstanding emphasis on trust and safety remains critical as its models become increasingly powerful. He joins Ed Ludlow and Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Joanna Stern on Siri’s iOS 27 Issues and Her Viral ‘Apple Dad’ Review
item.description: Joanna Stern joins Mark Gurman on the Power On podcast to discuss her frustrations testing Siri in iOS 27 and why dressing up as an “Apple Dad” sent her review viral. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Gets Win in User Data Court Case Against UK Government
item.description: A UK court has rejected the British government’s attempt to keep secret an order it sent to Apple Inc. seeking access to the encrypted data of customers.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: The Biggest Winners in Anthropic’s Landmark Public Offering
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday is expected to bring billions of dollars in returns to several financial firms that have bet the house on the Claude chatbot maker.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence
